claims.text: Tailored spark plasma sintering can consolidate a refractory-alloy-and-Cu powder mixture into a composite.
Rapid heating, high pressure, and an inert atmosphere during SPS enable a large-scale reaction between refractory alloy powders and Cu.
The proposed SPS process produces a stable Cu-containing composite microstructure despite positive refractory-element–Cu mixing enthalpy.
The starting powder mixture contains refractory high-entropy-alloy elements and copper.
A high positive enthalpy of mixing makes the refractory elements and Cu prone to phase segregation.
The SPS treatment uses rapid heating and high-pressure ramps under an inert atmosphere.
Rapid heating and sustained high pressure minimize diffusion time and control reaction kinetics.
SPS creates a refined, rapidly consolidated microstructure.
The rapidly consolidated microstructure suppresses diffusion-driven segregation between Cu and refractory elements.
Positive heat of mixing drives equilibrium phase separation in the proposed refractory-alloy–Cu system.
Limiting the time available for equilibrium separation allows SPS to preserve a uniform composite microstructure.
The proposed process produces a dense, large-scale composite with a uniformly reacted microstructure.
The SPS composite has better mechanical properties than conventionally processed composites.
The SPS composite has better irradiation resistance than conventionally processed composites.
Conventional processing allows longer diffusion times that cause phase segregation and unstable microstructures.
The effectiveness of SPS may depend on composite thickness, Cu proportion, and the heating and pressure profiles.
